We have applied first template 324324, got precursors: product? The result tuple: ('Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1', 'Nc1ccccc1N'). So first reaction splits the amide? Actually original target had ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. The template likely breaks the amide to give an aniline (Nc1ccccc1N) and a carboxylic acid derivative.

Now second template 1914396 applied to the first precursor (the sulfonyl phenyl with carboxylic acid). It gave ('Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1', 'O=C(O)CC(=O)O'). So we have a benzaldehyde (C=O) attached to sulfonyl phenyl, and a dicarboxylic acid (oxalic acid? Actually O=C(O)CC(=O)O is malonic acid). Good.

Now third template 733 to apply to which molecule? Probably to the aldehyde fragment to generate something simpler. Need to apply template 733 to 'Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1' maybe to break the sulfonyl? Or to the malonic acid? Let's check applicability. Use check for each.
